FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Part 3) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Marine Instruments and Safety Aids Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. Pyrotechnic distress signals form parts of the lifeboats andliferaftsequipment Rules, 1986 under the Merchant ShippingAct, 1958, in accordance with Life

SavingAppliances

The Indian Standards covering the whole range of pyrotechnic distress signals are being published in the following parts: Shipbuilding - Pyrotechnic distress signals for ships: Part Part Part Part Part Part Part Part 1 2 4 5 6 7 8 9 General requirements Red flare parachute signal White flare signal White flare parachute signal Explosive shell signal Explosive rocket signal Orange smoke signal Red flare signal 3 107.9-1982 `Standards of pyrotechnic signals for ships', issued

These standards are based on GB 3107.1by the China State Bureau of Standard.

The composition of the committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex A. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : I960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 14270 ( Part 3 ) : 1997

Indian Standard

SHIPBUILDING - PYROTECHNIC DISTRESS SIGNALS FOR SHIPS
PART 3 RED STAR ROCKET SIGNAL SPECIFICATION

1 SCOPE This standard (Part 3) specifies sizes, materials and tests for red star rocket signal for use in ships when they are in distress and need help, by the rescue stations or Marine emergency service units to guide those in distress ships, distress boats and rafts to land. Its performance conforms to stipulations of SOLAS convention 1974 and International Marine regulations for preventing collisions at sea, 1972. 2 REFERENCE IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995 `Shipbuilding Pyrotechnic distress signals for ships : Part 1 General requirements' is a necessary adjunct to this Standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard definitions given in IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995 shall apply. 4 FORM AND SIZE 4.1 Red star rocket signal for ships is the flare type signal which is driven forward by rockets and ignited either by pulling or by striking. Its main components include:

a) b)
4

Flare strength of not less than SO 000 candela (cd) ; Flare duration of not less than 8 seconds; and Red flare colour as per the diagram stipulated by International Illumination Committee, area limit of its chromaticity shall be within the scope of following co-ordinates: x Y 0.680 0.320 0.660 0.320 0.735 0.265 0.721 0.259

5.3 Signal chemical sticks shall be made of gun powder, ignition chemicals, signal chemical, etc, its outer diameter shall not exceed 35 mm and total weight shall not be less than 80 g. 5.4 Rocket launcher is made up of rocket body, gun powder, propellant and outer shell, etc. Outer shell shall be aluminium tube of outer diameter not less than 38 mm, the diameter of the nozzle of the steel rocket body shall be suitable for the propellant. On the upper side of the rocket body the signal chemical sticks are placed. 5.5 Ignition device shall conform to the stipulation of 4.1 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 5.6 Shell and direction tube shall be made of plastic or equivalent material. 5.7 Connecting item and handle shall be made of plastic or equivalent material, its one end is connected to the signal shell and the other to the safety cap. 5.8 Safety cap and top cap is made of plastic or metal, its height not being more than 2.5 mm, its outer surface shall have knurling and be red in colour. Metal cap shall undergo anti-corrosive treatment. 5.9 The outer shape and composition of the signal shall conform to the stipulations of 4.2 of IS 13270 (Part 1) : 1995. 5.10 The signal, in release condition without the safety cap, shall bc immersed in 10 cm deep water for one minute and its utility performanceshall not be affected. 1

f-l

Ignition device, Shell and guiding tube, Connecting item, and Safety cap and top cap.

4.2 Outer diameter of the red star rocket signal for ships shall not be more than 45 mm and total length shall not exceed 270 mm. Its total weight shall not exceed 440 g. 5 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS AND GENERAL

5.1 Red star rocket signal for ships shall conform to IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 5.2 This signal after igniting by pulling or by striking shall be driven into the air by rocket to a height of not less than 300 m, to give out red flare, having:

IS 14270 ( Part 3 ) : 1997
5.11 When subjected to a salt spray (20 percent sodium chloride solution) at a temperature of 35+3"C for at least 100 h the signal shall function effectively. 5.12 The signal while igniting shall not have any blind fire, explosion or mishap. Rocket shall be safe and dependable, its initial thrust shall be proper and the igniting flame shall not burn the hand of the person releasing it.

out. During the release test also, the flame duration time shall be noted down for comparison. 6.2.3 The flare strength and flame duration of each batch of products is taken separately to calculate the average value of each test samples. 6.3 Flare Chromaticity Test Flare chromaticity is measured by using calorimeter in the flare chromaticity, area limit or under the sunlight by the measurement method, using human eyes in which standard red colour sample with plates, as per the stipulations of 5.2 of this standard are compared with its colour. 6.4 Launching Height Test The height of the rocket launched is measured at the test field or at the time of release on ship, by using height measuring equipment. Its height is measured from the launching place to the place where the red star flame is just stationary. 6.5 Release Test Release test may be conducted on the special launcher, but at least one signal shall be released by hand. 6.6 Vibration test, dropping test, low temperature test, high temperature test and general performance test of the signal shall conform to the stipulations 5.2 to 5.5 and 5.8 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 7 INSPECTION

5.13 The signal, when freely dropped on a steel plate from a height of 3 m, shall not ignite or explode and its utility performance shall not be affected. 5.14 The test for the validity period of the signal shall conform to the stipulation as in 6.4 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 6 TESTING 6.1 Test methods of the signal shall conform to the stipulations of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995. 6.2 Flare Strength and Duration Test Determination of the flare strength shall be done by using `ST' type or equivalent lux meter, under the test lab conditions of simulated black body and wind speed of 5 m/s. After igniting, 3-4 values are taken and after calculating its average value the result shall be arrived at , as per the following formula:

8 MARKING 8.1 The packing container of every shell and finished goods of the signal products and its shipment packing cases shall conform to the requirements stipulated in 7 of IS 14270 (part 1) : 1995. 8.2 Operation parameter of the product shall also include the flare strength and duration and the height to which the rocket is launched. It shall not be directed against the person who releases it.

9 PACKlNG Packing of the signal product shall conform to the stipulations as in 8 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 199.5. 10 STORAGE Storage of the signal product shall conform to the stipulations as in 9 of IS 14270 (Part 1) : 1995.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods. and attending to connected matters in the country. Copy&b t

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Dot: No. TED 20 ( 936 ).
